time warp.text: This deck can finish the game with a strong combo including its main champion and Time Warp . However, it is struggling to adapt to the current competitive meta. It's great in Nexus Nights, particularly to steal wins from unaware players, because its greatest advantage is that no one knows how it works. So, let's see it!

This is a control/combo list centered around Holding battlefields. The main idea is to score as many points as possible early on, hold a battlefield, and hoard Gold Gear Tokens in your base. Eventually, you'll have enough resources to play Time Warp , often multiple times in a row, and Ekko - Recurrent and win the game.

The main champion, Renata Glasc - Mastermind , is essential because her effect scores points. Depending on your final board, you can play Time Warp and use Renata Glasc - Mastermind 's effect all in the same turn and win.

Renata Glasc is a late game legend that doubles how much power your Gold Gear Tokens give you if you have 5 points or more. This is essential for the main combo because then you'll be able to play Time Warp stress-free and use your main champion on the same turn or right afterward.
Only use its second effect if you already have Time Warp + Ekko + Hidden Blade and many Gold Gear Tokens . Otherwise, only use its first effect to look for your combo pieces.
The main combo involves playing Time Warp several times to Hold battelfields twice or multiple times in a row.
To play Time Warp twice in a row, you must have 12 runes, at least 1 Gold Gear Tokens in your base, an Ekko - Recurrent in play, and a Hidden Blade or Deathgrip in your hand.

However, you'll often have to combine Time Warp with Renata Glasc - Mastermind 's second effect. To do that, you'll need the same cards as above, plus 2 Gold Gear Tokens in your base and Renata Glasc - Mastermind on a battlefield. With this setup, you can play a Time Warp and use Renata's effect on the same turn.
To play Time Warp , use Renata 's effect, and, on the following turn, use Renata 's effect again, you'll need to have at least 4 Gold Gear Token in your base.

Cut by half the number of Gold Gear Tokens you need to play this combo if you already have 5 or more points. For instance: you only need 2 Gold Gears to use Time Warp and Renata 's effect twice if you have 5 or more points.
Spells: Removal spells: Singularity , Icathian Rain or event Unchecked Power , fillers for main deck combat tricks and even taking turns by Time Warp

Let's circle back to what we talked about in the introduction about the mind domain's role in the metagame, switching from a strong card draw support to instead provide more ways to cheat energy. No card embodies this change more than SFD-083 , or as some have started to call it : Time Warp on a gear.
Time Warp, two. "Take a turn after this one." 10 Energy and 4 power, so it's a late-game finisher, not something you plan around early.

Hush. A Radiance Reaction spell that counters a spell with a Power cost of 2 or more. In piorro's list, that's three Falling Star and two Time Warp. A long-time Kai'Sa player, u/Lowe5521, flagged it in the same Reddit thread: "it hits Singularity, Falling Star, Icathian Rain AND Time Warp." Your cheap spells (Hextech Ray, Stupefy, Smoke Screen, Bellows Breath, Temporal Breach) cost 1 power or none, so Hush can't counter them.

Kai'Sa, Survivor's cheapest copy is the Origins alternate art; the regular Epic is $67.68. Time Warp, Watcher and Falling Star only sell as foils. All four went up between October 24 and 29: Time Warp was $44.14 and Falling Star $10.19 when we first priced the list. Bilgewater Tracker is $0.11, The Empyrean $0.12 and Lost to the Sands $0.14. The Radiance cards are the cheap part.

Don't let riftbound.gg's $866 scare you off. Buy the common Plundering Poro, and the real cost is about $334, most of it in two Time Warp and one Kai'Sa, Survivor. Thirteen players is a small sample, so read our Radiance tier list for where Kai'Sa stands against the other Legends, and expect this list to change once the in-person season starts.

hostile takeover.text: The main idea early on is to mulligan after your 2-costs and Card Sharp . You must also keep Hostile Takeover in hand because it's critical. With it, you'll transition to your main Holding strategy after you get 5 points.

Hostile Takeover is also essential. With it, you'll defend your board from attacks with multiple units. Keep in mind that you can't take control of an enemy unit that is on another battlefield if you play Hidden Hostile Takeover . This card, by itself, destroys any enemy attack and puts a lot of pressure on the opponent. It also disrupts their strategy.

draven + point.text: The main limiting for Draven is the lack of a strong champion unit early on in a match. Indeed, OGN-039 requires at least 4 points to be scored in order to be a threat, most of the time limiting the appeal to play it on curve. As a result, fast-paced decks, or those able to quickly remove a 4-might unit anywhere on the board will be a problem Draven as the legend doesn't fare well when forced to play from behind.
Unfortunately, you don't have great chances against Draven because the units in this list are bigger than yours, and they also play control tools to get points early on.

Draven Audacious is a potential win condition, especially in slow matchups. If Draven Audacious wins a combat, you get to gain a Point from him, accelerating your goal to 8 Points. Keep in mind that if you're at 6 Points and haven't conquered both battlefields, you can't win the game through Draven's +1 Point score ability. If Draven wins a combat while you're at 6 Points, you will first trigger his ability to push you to 7 Points, and then the battlefield conquer will get you the other point, so if you haven't conquered or held the other battlefield, you'll get a card draw instead.
If Draven dies in combat, you will be giving your opponent 1 Point, but if you have Guardian Angel attached to him, you can dodge the drawback.

baited hook.text: In Vendetta, the Grand Duelist found success with all three concepts in different tournaments. The Baited Hook deck started strong with a top 16 in Barcelona, then the midrange deck reached the top 4 in Wuhan, followed by an Aurora deck able to switch to midrange making it to Singapore's top 8. Baited Hook packs a bigger punch, able to win matches on the back of sheer proactive power. Aurora follows the same idea, but tends to be even more committed to finding its gear. On the other hand, midrange lists tend to be more flexible and able to interact with the opponent. Plus, they also avoid the annoying issue of gear removal destroying their key card.

Aurora tends to play its own game, with a large emphasis on its own agenda. As for Baited Hook or Midrange decks, both want to seize the board and keep the opponent at bay from there. Fiora's early game isn't fantastic, but once she gained a few runes through her legend ability, or simply equipped SFD-161 without losing a rune, she is difficult to manoeuvre. Indeed, her signature spell SFD-206 is fantastic while she packs plenty of ways to edge a showdown or take out opposing units.

OGN-242 requires the deck to be built around units with scaling might to be effective while OGN-160 focuses on late game threats and packs early ramp like OGN-134 . On the other hand, the midrange list is more flexible and will focus on strong standalone cards a lot more. In both the Baited Hook and Midrange decks, we find similar support cards to help with buffing our units or take care of opposite ones.

Considering RAD-020 possesses 5-might and an ability to keep him alive once per turn, cards with 4 and 6 should be excellent in a Baited Hook deck. This, I have my eyes on OGN-012 , SFD-176 or OGN-226 for the first group and OGN-234 , SFD-179 or SFD-021 for more expensive units.

In my opinion, Kennen's ability wants to build around the Miracle play style. First, it is the most logical route in order to consistently trigger it, although Baited Hook can also work. Then, I feel like it is the most flexible way to build Kennen early on. Not only the deck has room to make swaps and adapt to the metagame in the future, it also is a proactive strategy with fantastic value tools. Thus, Kennen is able to push its own agenda while the environment features a bit of everything, but will be able to adapt once the first tournaments point at the best legends in Vendetta.

It might be Fiora's track record, or the fact I feel the Empower synergy is too expensive to develop, but I can't build Embessa without OGN-242 . I know, I said building around a gear was too risky in Jayce's review, while Kennen's Baited Hook build didn't appeal to me either. Yet, without the 3-cost gear to help us cheat energy, I struggle to see how does Embessa manage to develop new units while empowering the ones on the board in the same turn. On the other hand, her ability is just perfect with OGN-242 , as we can ready the new unit we summoned every turn.

Jhin is a meticulous criminal psychopath who believes murder is art. Once an Ionian prisoner, but freed by shadowy elements within Ionia's ruling council, the serial killer now works as their cabal's assassin. Using his gun as his paintbrush, Jhin creates works of artistic brutality, horrifying victims and onlookers. He gains a cruel pleasure from putting on his gruesome theater, making him the ideal choice to send the most powerful of messages: terror.

Jhin is a combo oriented legend, designed to win without scoring points, but through UNL-088 instead. As a result, Jhin is one of the few legends in Riftbound able to ignore the scoreboard as long as the opponent isn't getting close to 8 points. Consider their progression on the scoreboard as the clock the Virtuoso needs to keep in mind to progress towards its own win condition.

Typically, the start of the game will be quite slow for Jhin, who wants to keep gaining runes, draw cards and simply remove opposing units as they come during the first three or four turns of the match. All those cards should cost 4 or more to interact with the legend's ability, a key part of setting up the combo later.

Once in the later stages, Jhin will combine four cards to grab the win. UNL-088 is the win condition. OGN-026 prevents the opponent from interacting with our shenanigans, removing counter spells from the equation. OGN-110 is our runes engine we'll simply sacrifice into any opposing unit able to kill it, or even use our own spell to help with that process. Last, OGN-122 will give us another turn, to immediately win the game if we built the right set up.
I feel like learning the deck from its creator will be the best way, so if you are fine with a video, here is a breakdown of the entire Gutter Palace Jhin deck .
Play spells to load our legend. Without the 4 extra runes Jhin channels with its ability, it is difficult to reach 12 runes in time.

This progression limits Jhin's opportunity to recycle runes early in the match. UNL-073 will help with that, while OGN-120 can be played once we reached six runes and played OGN-114 , to avoid future power costs.

However, Jhin suddenly turned things around in the western metagame over the last two regional tournaments, Utrecht and Hartford. There, the Mind - Fury legend post a Top 64 followed by a Top 32, his two best results by a mile.

This was both way too late and not enough to make Jhin a competitive threat, especially as the results in the Chinese metagame didn't change, with a clean record sheet of four top 256. Yet, it makes Jhin a lot more interesting heading into Vendetta, especially with Kai'Sa not granting best-of cards in the future, or a new Mind - Fury joining the roster in the new expansion.

void gate.text: When it comes to Battlefields, everything is basically decided. The most frequently chosen Battlefields ( Void Gate and Targon's Peak ) fit very well into the deck's strategy. Currently, the third most frequently chosen Battlefield is Reaver's Row , which allows us to avoid losing our defender.

Runes: 7 Fury, 5 Mind. Battlefields: Void Gate, Rockfall Path, Frozen Fortress. Sideboard (10): two each of Brittle Steel, Decree of Rage and Decree of Insight, and one each of Hextech Ray, Icathian Rain, Lost to the Sands and Ferrous Forerunner.
Void Gate: "Spells and abilities affecting units here each deal 1 Bonus Damage." Falling Star becomes 4 and 4 there, and Hextech Ray deals 4.
Count to 4 Might. Tracker's 1 damage on two units lets Falling Star's two 3s kill both. At Void Gate, Falling Star kills two 4-Might units on its own.

rumble + mech.text: Rumble, Mechanized Menace Guide - Best Decks & Cards - Riftbound TCG
Rumble, Mechanized Menace Guide – Best Decks & Cards
Your guide to Rumble, Mechanized Menace Legend in Riftbound TCG: Overview of its meta status, sample decks, cards, and synergies.

Rumble is a young inventor with a temper. Using nothing more than his own two hands and a heap of scrap, the feisty yordle constructed a colossal mech suit outfitted with an arsenal of electrified harpoons and incendiary rockets. Though others may scoff and sneer at his junkyard creations, Rumble doesn't mind—after all, he's the one with the flamespitter.

Rumble inherited of the same domains as Kai'Sa , arguably the greatest legend in Riftbound heading into Spiritforged, and still a fantastic performer in this new metagame. In comparison, being forced to play a tribe focused synergy is a huge limitation, both in terms of cards we can run, but also the information we give our opponent when revealing our legend. As such, SFD-181 will see restricted play except when Mechs are able to dominate an opponent fully aware of our strategy from the very start of the match.

In this dream scenario, Rumble is then able to snowball that position and score points regularly. SFD-026 comes as an additional threat to deal with, mechs are being summoned, buffed, and the deck just clicks. Unfortunately, an educated opponent will play against that outcome, while going second means we can't really follow this pattern.

Finding a way to summon SFD-021 early on through SFD-026 is the best way for Rumble to pressure its opponent and score consistently. Another great card to summon mechs at a discount is SFD-076 , always a 2-cost card in this deck. Alongside our champion units, the deck is looking for those tools, able to develop our side of the board for cheap or present cards requiring more resources to remove than we used to get them in play.

teemo + hidden.text: Once in the lead, Teemo will use hidden cards to keep the opponent guessing on the best way to navigate the situation. In that confusion, it is important to score every turn, building even more pressure as the scoreboard gets closer to 8. Eventually, the opponent will be forced to take risks, and fall into one of our traps.
Teemo had a strong month of May, appearing as a reliable day 2 competitor thanks to new hidden cards, and a metagame rewarding legends able to go at a hundred miles an hour early on.

At first glance, Vendetta appears to feature mostly synergistic legends, with most abilities and cards related to each legend geared towards a specific play style. Akali - Rogue Assassin wants to move, Renekton - Butcher of the Sands to cheat out energy, Nasus - Curator of the Sands to Ramp, Zed - Master of Shadows to banish cards, Kennen - Heart of the Tempest to special summon, Ambessa - Matriarch of War and Mel - Soul's Reflection look to Empower…
Renekton is the most unbalanced legend in Vendetta without a doubt. However, I must say I'll have to play it more to figure out whether the unbalance goes in the right or the wrong way.

However, there is also the bad start scenario. In that one, we have to use our legend ability to catch up, and basically pray the opponent cannot remove our unit or we'll be stuck hoping the next one sticks to the board. We have ways to answer the board with OGN-029 , but every strong play Renekton can do requires to recycle runes.

Early on, I expect Renekton to get a few social media posts from people about high rolls, still fuming how broken certain patterns look like. However, I wonder how it will fare over hundreds of game, or if the Seals get destroyed early on.

zhonya.text: The Hidden mechanic appears on Tideturner , Zhonya's Hourglass , Fight or Flight , and Switcheroo . These cards can be played face-down for a rainbow rune, then flipped up later for zero energy as reactions. This creates enormous tempo swings—you're developing board presence or setting up protection while keeping mana available for other plays. Tideturner in particular is deceptively powerful: a 2-energy 2-might unit with Chaos typing that you can hide early and flip during combat to surprise block or trigger movement synergies.

This list runs several expensive cards—Defiant Dance, Guardian Angel, Zhonya's Hourglass, and the champion suite all carry premium price tags. If you're building on a budget, here's where you can compromise without destroying the deck's functionality.

Now with the bodies on board to deal with all the removal, Schorn kept one trick up his sleeve: Equipment. With favorable colors, Yi does have access to Guardian Angel and Zhonya’s Hourglass for survival, as well as Brutalizer and Trinity Force for big might swings. Couple that with a legend ability contingent on defending, and you can get big holds to swing the tempo in your favour.

“Typically they play it in the second game, so I pull my gear out for the second game and then surprise them with Forge in the third game, putting all my gear back in including Brutalizer. I keep Zhonya’s in, but when they have their Thermo Beams and Salvages in hand for second game, they can’t really use it efficiently. They then side it out for Game 3, so when I need the gear for my Forge game, I put it back in.”

Zhonya's Hourglass acts similarly to Guardian Angel, protecting one of your units from getting killed. Zhonya's Hourglass has its advantages, as you don't have to recycle a rune and attach it to Irelia to protect her. However, you lose the Might boost that Guardian Angel provides.
Zhonya's Hourglass, three. OGN-077 OGN-077 Shop on TCGplayer Zhonya's Hourglass saves the next friendly unit that would die and recalls it to base. Riven, Broken Blade is the unit you'd want saved.
8 Chaos runes; +3 Traveling Merchant, +3 Treasure Hunter, +2 Zed, +2 Baron Nashor; no Astral Heron, Bedeviling Stranger or Zhonya's

unyielding spirit.text: Your worst matchup, though not unwinnable. You're spending your early turns channelling runes while they're deploying threats and attacking. Challenge and Called Shot are your primary defensive tools. Prioritise removing their most efficient threats and stabilising around turn four or five. Volibear, Imposing is your best card in this matchup—once he lands, aggressive decks struggle to push through. Post-board, you bring in Unyielding Spirit to protect key blockers and Gust to bounce their biggest threats.

nocturne.text: However, you can do that if your hand is too clunky. This doesn't happen with this list often, but it is possible. Particularly, you might just not draw your Nocturne - Horrifying .

Nocturne - Horrifying might seem counterintuitive in this deck because usually we'll usually draw cards when we take a look at the top of our deck. However, Nocturne - Horrifying will help you stay ahead in tempo in critical moments, that is, when drawing cards wouldn't make that much of a difference.

Just drawing cards isn't enough, though. You must assess the board state and play Nocturne only when you need to put units in play. Keep in mind that your units are relatively weak compared to other units in the meta right now.
If you draw Nocturne - Horrifying , he'll be the perfect card to discard with Zaun Warrens or Traveling Merchant .

Kai'Sa can control your units, but you'll be faster. If you play lots of units on the board, like 3 Rhasa and some Nocturnes , you can strangle her. That's why, in this matchup, you must set up a very explosive turn. You only have one chance to win. If Kai'Sa destroys your units, you'll hardly be able to build your board back.

Practically all cards in this sideboard are great replacements for Nocturne , considering many players don't like playing him. Ride the Wind and On the Hunt are great alternatives for him in any matchup.
Riven emerges as the new threat from Radiance. Kai'Sa positions herself as the Riven counter. Kennen gets Nocturne and his power back. Akali offers a versatile option.

After the bans in Vendetta, it took some time for Kennen to bounce back and return to a Tier 1 status. The main problem the legend had to overcome was the loss of OGN-194 coming in for cheap to anchor the early game. Radiance solved that issue with RAD-129 , allowing Nocturne to come back in the mix and Kennen to look like a powerhouse once again.

IHATECOFFEE's list is the other real build. It swaps the big Calm units for Chaos units that pay off moving: Treasure Hunter makes a Gold gear token when it moves, and Traveling Merchant discards and draws. If you're short on Astral Herons, that's the version to try.

Each turn you channel 2 runes, and the Core Rules give the player going second one extra rune on their first turn. A rune can be exhausted for 1 Energy or recycled for a power of its Domain. That puts Riven, Broken Blade (4) on turn 2 either way, and Astral Heron (7) on turn 3 going second and turn 4 going first.
